chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Sa'd ibn Sa'd al-Ash'ari, from Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about the Fitrah (alms of breaking the fast), how much should be paid for every head from wheat, barley, dates, and raisins? He said: A sa' with the sa' of the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family).

key_terms.التَّمْر: Dates, one of the staple foods for Zakat al-Fitr
key_terms.الزَّبِيب: Raisins, one of the staple foods for Zakat al-Fitr
key_terms.الشَّعِير: Barley, one of the staple foods for Zakat al-Fitr
key_terms.الْحِنْطَة: Wheat, one of the staple foods for Zakat al-Fitr
key_terms.الْفِطْرَة: Zakat al-Fitr, the obligatory charity given at the end of Ramadan
key_terms.بِصَاعِ النَّبِيِّ: According to the measure of the Prophet, indicating the standard volume used during his time
key_terms.صَاعٌ: A sa', a traditional unit of volume used for measuring Zakat al-Fitr

ai.seo_question: What is the prescribed amount and type of food for Zakat al-Fitr in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Rida (AS) in *Al-Istibsar* clarifies the specific volume of one *sa'* for Zakat al-Fitr, linking the practice directly to the Prophetic tradition to ensure consistency in ritual obligation. It highlights the Shia emphasis on adhering to the exact measures prescribed by the Ahl al-Bayt, reinforcing the continuity of Islamic jurisprudence from the Prophet's time. This specification ensures the charity fulfills its social welfare purpose by providing a tangible, standardized amount of staple food to the needy.
